a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

b.label: State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons

edges.label: AAWSAP deliverable; the only one with a classified version
edges.note: The released document names the programme itself. Its inside cover reads 'This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency ... Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program' - the redaction between them is (b)(3):10 USC 424. Verified by downloading this DIRD and scanning its full text on 23 August 2026. The scans are OCR-degraded, so the quotation is normalised from the damaged rendering.

a.label: Biosensors and BioMEMS: A Survey of the Present Field

edges.label: authored by Bruce Towe
edges.note: Attribution rests on the DIA list of 38 AATIP products transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee on 9 January 2018, entry 6: 'Biosensors and BioMEMS, Dr Bruce Towe, Univ of Arizona.' The released PDF's own author block is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(5), so the DIA list is the sole authority for authorship. Towe also wrote the 'Biomaterials' DIRD (entry 17).

a.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft

edges.label: authored by Richard J. Genik II
edges.note: The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records 'Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(6). Genik wrote three of the 38 DIRDs, the largest single-author block after Eric Davis's five.

a.label: Cognitive Limits on Simultaneous Control of Multiple Unmanned Spacecraft

edges.label: author's institution at time of writing
edges.note: Genik was director of the Emergent Technology Research Division and assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neurosciences at the Wayne State University School of Medicine. Wayne State supplied four of the 38 DIRDs across two authors - Genik's three plus Kit Green's 'Field Effects on Biological Tissues' - the second-largest institutional concentration after EarthTech International's six.

edges.label: authored
edges.note: DIA list item 11 names "Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech International". Independently confirmed by EarthTech International's own publication list, which cites the document as Davis, E. W. (2010) with document number DIA-08-1003-018 and originating office Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3), Defense Warning Office.

b.label: Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list and on EarthTech's own citation list
edges.note: DIA list item 8: "Traversable Wormholes, Stargates and Negative Energy, Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech International." Unlike the warp-drive paper, the popular attribution to Davis is confirmed by the government list here. EarthTech's own bibliography carries the same citation with the document number DIA-08-1004-004.

b.label: The Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: DIA list item 10: "Role of Superconductors in Gravity Research, Dr George Hathaway, Hathaway Consulting." This is the attribution most likely to be got wrong from the title alone: the paper reviews the Podkletnov and Ning Li gravity-modification claims but was not written by either of them or by any academic advocate of the effect. It was written by the Toronto engineer who had run the Podkletnov replication and reported null results.

edges.label: authored by George H. Miley, University of Illinois
edges.note: Entry 1 on both the KLAS list of July 2018 and the DIA letter of 9 January 2018: 'Inertial Electrostatics Confinement Fusion, Dr George Miley, Univ. of Illinois.' The released PDF's author block is redacted under (b)(5). Miley is co-author of the Springer monograph on IEC fusion, making him a documented subject-matter authority rather than a fringe recruit.

edges.label: subject domain: compact non-tokamak fusion power
edges.note: IEC is one of the few AAWSAP topics with a plausible conventional aerospace reading: a compact fusion device is what a small craft would need if it were producing the observed energy budget. The DIRD set contains four fusion-adjacent deliverables in total - Miley's IEC paper, Winterberg's advanced nuclear propulsion, Teofilo's aneutronic fusion propulsion for Lockheed Martin, and Culbreth's aneutronic fusion propulsion II.

b.label: State of the Art and Evolution of High-Energy Laser Weapons

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list, both versions
edges.note: The DIA letter lists this paper twice, items 37 and 38, both credited to J Albertine of Directed Technologies: one formerly classified SECRET//NOFORN, one unclassified. The board node is labelled with the initial because no source consulted confirms the given name; the probable identification with John R. Albertine of the Navy High Energy Laser Program Office is carried as a tier-3 claim on the person node.

b.label: Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: DIA list item 35: "Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices, Dr J Golightly, Lockheed Martin." The given name behind the initial was not established by any source consulted, and the node is labelled accordingly rather than guessed.

b.label: The Space-Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: DIA list item 25: "Space_Communication Implications of Quantum Entanglement and Nonlocality, Dr J Cramer, Univ of Washington." A mainstream university physicist, not a programme insider.

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA list of all 38 AATIP/AAWSAP products, transmitted to the Senate Armed Services Committee in January 2018 and released under FOIA in January 2019, credits 'Laser Lightcraft Nanosatellites' to 'Dr E Davis, EarthTech'. The author line on the released PDF cover page is redacted, so this attribution rests on the congressional list rather than the document.

a.label: MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications' to 'Dr S Macheret, Lockheed Martin'. Macheret is a plasma physicist (Ph.D., Kurchatov Institute) with a substantial peer-reviewed record in MHD flow control, and this DIRD is among the most conventionally grounded on the list.

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Negative Mass Propulsion' to 'Dr F Winterberg, Univ of Nevada-Reno'. Winterberg is also credited on the same list with 'Advanced Nuclear Propulsion for Manned Deep Space Missions', and published related negative-mass propulsion work in the Journal of the British Interplanetary Society in 2011.

b.label: Space Access: Where We've Been and Where We Could Go

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: The DIA letter of 9 January 2018 to the Senate Armed Services Committee lists item 4 as "Space Access, Dr P Czysz, HyperTech." The released document's own author line is redacted under FOIA exemption (b)(6), so the attribution rests entirely on the government list, not on the document.

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Pulsed High-Power Microwave Technology' to 'Dr James Wells, J W Enterprises'. The earlier Knapp/KLAS-TV roster gives the same author with the affiliation Northrop Grumman; the DIA list governs. No verified biography for this author has been located beyond the list entry.

a.label: Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Quantum Computing and Utilizing Organic Molecules in Automation Technology' to 'Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ'. Genik is credited elsewhere on the same list with the brain-machine interface deliverable on controlling external devices without limb-operated interfaces, making him a multi-product AAWSAP contributor.

a.label: Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum

edges.label: authored by
edges.note: The DIA congressional list credits 'Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum' to 'Dr Eric Davis, EarthTech'. This is one of a coherent negative-energy sub-series by the same author within the DIRD set, alongside 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates and Negative Energy' and the quantum-vacuum energy extraction paper.

edges.label: co-affiliated AAWSAP authors at Wayne State University
edges.note: The DIA congressional list records Wayne State University as the affiliation for both Genik's deliverables and for Kit Green's human biological tissue field-effects deliverable. This establishes a documented shared institutional affiliation on the same contract, not a documented working relationship — no primary source describing collaboration between them has been located, and the edge should not be read as one.

b.label: Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list
edges.note: DIA list item 20: "Technological Applications to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces, Dr R Genik, Wayne State Univ." The KLAS-TV list of July 2018 gives the same document the plainer title "Brain-Machine Interfaces."

b.label: Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions

edges.label: author of record on the DIA list; lead author
edges.note: CORRECTION EDGE. The DIA letter of 9 January 2018, item 19, names "Dr R Obousy, Obousy Consultants" as the author of the warp-drive DIRD. Press coverage almost universally attributes this paper to Eric Davis. EarthTech's own citation gives it as Obousy, R. K. and Davis, E. W. (2010), with Obousy first named, so the two records reconcile as a co-authored paper on which DIA recorded the lead author.

a.label: Technological Approaches to Controlling External Devices in the Absence of Limb-Operated Interfaces

edges.label: author's affiliation of record
edges.note: Wayne State is the DIA-listed affiliation for four DIRDs: Genik's three human-factors papers and Kit Green's "Field Effects on Biological Tissues." That makes it the single most productive institution in the DIRD set after EarthTech International, and the locus of the programme's human-effects line of inquiry.

a.label: Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy

b.label: EarthTech International / Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin

edges.label: author's affiliation of record; DIRD carried on EarthTech's own publications list
edges.note: EarthTech International lists six DIRDs by Eric Davis on its publications page, with DIA document numbers and the issuing division named as the Acquisition Support Division (DWO-3) or Technology Warning Division (DWO-4) of the Defense Warning Office. A contractor publishing its DIA reference-document numbers on an open website is itself part of how the DIRD series became documentable.

a.label: Ultracapacitors as Energy and Power Storage Devices for Commercial and Military Applications

edges.label: author's affiliation of record; one of three Lockheed Martin DIRDs
edges.note: Lockheed Martin appears three times on the DIA list: this paper, Dr V Teofilo's "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion," and Dr S Macheret's MHD air-breathing propulsion paper. Eric Davis said in a June 2018 interview that the advanced nuclear fusion for aerospace propulsion work was done by colleagues at Lockheed Martin, which matches the list. This is a direct, documented thread from the DIRD series into the prime-contractor cluster.
